findings: Per-platform Work/FSM journals already exist, but group CBE_ArtilleryCrew_Reference stores exactly one [platform,token,serial,epoch,owner] tuple. Start refuses any existing tuple and then publishes its own; Current and Step require exact singleton equality.

CortexOwnershipLease also refuses acquisition while any artillery reference exists, even for ARTILLERY_CREW. Its one public [owner,server-expiry] lease and the private group movementLease cannot represent independent per-gun retirement or deadlines.

Live Step finalization releases the group lease and clears the singleton. Shared VehicleCrewMoveRetire does the same after positive native return/STOP or original-crew-loss/rest proof; its adoption rewrites the singleton for the new epoch. A second admission alone would strand the first worker or let one terminal path remove a peer reservation.

CortexDiscover and locality gain service one referenced platform. Locality loss removes one platform deletion observer. CortexStop adopts retirement for one platform. All must service exact admitted entries before widening admission.

VehicleCrewMoveDeletionWatch captures one exact reference, original crew and exact public-lease snapshot. Deleted platform references can become null; a future multi-entry identity must remain unambiguous after deletion rather than relying on object existence or assuming token/serial uniqueness across platforms.

CortexArtilleryScoot treats any group crew reference as this battery prefire retirement. A peer-aware path must distinguish this gun from another gun, retaining the original scoot deadline rather than cancelling or retiring the wrong job.

DrivingMovementAvailable, CortexGroupTick and VehicleTacticalMoveStart reserve the whole movement domain while a reference remains. Non-artillery group movement must remain blocked while any unresolved selected-gun native work remains; do not interpret lease expiry as quiescence.

NativeOrderReceipt observes group waypoint metadata only. It does not itself change when another gun receives a per-actor move, so the waypoint receipt is not the cause of current peer refusal. The shared native kernel separately checks original actor destinations before writes and refuses replaced destinations; keep those checks.
